notes: Privilege and prohibition map directly; asset.quality.errorRate becomes the state property ex:feedErrorRate (xsd:decimal, exact). RL2 puts the conflict strategy in configuration; odrl:prohibit is made explicit, and it never decides an outcome here because the two constraints are complementary. The independent RL2 duty becomes a root odrl:obligation. Its constraint reads a state operand, so it is a guard (due2-workflows.md §5.2): the obligation is in force when a rule of the policy matches the request — both the privilege and the prohibition match a Subscriber read — and the error rate exceeds 0.05. Its status is then reported with bearer ex:DataTeam, though the request subject is ex:Subscriber: at 0.08 it is outstanding, which is RL2's Active status-map entry for the independent duty. The duty's own action ex:report plays no part in in-force (§5.2). The access verdicts and the duty status agree with RL2. Monitoring the duty outside any request remains open (§9 #4) but no scenario needs it. Scenarios 3 and 4 are added.

expected.why: 0.02 ≤ 0.05 makes ex:readFeedPrivilege T, a ready candidate; 0.02 > 0.05 is F, so the prohibition does not apply. Both rules match the request, but the obligation's guard 0.02 > 0.05 is F, so it is not in force.

0.08 > 0.05 makes ex:poorQualityProhibition T and it survives; the permission is F. The prohibition matches the request and the obligation's guard 0.08 > 0.05 is T, so ex:reportIncidentDuty is in force; no ex:report by ex:DataTeam on ex:QualityIncident is in evidence, so it is outstanding (RL2: Active), with bearer ex:DataTeam. It does not affect the verdict (§6.1).

scenarios.name: error rate exactly at the threshold

expected.why: 0.050 and 0.05 are the same decimal value, so lteq is T and gt is F: the permission is ready and the prohibition does not apply. The obligation's guard is F, so it is not in force.

Both the permission and the prohibition are U. The restrictive completion (permission F, prohibition T) gives Deny; the permissive one (permission T, prohibition F) gives Permit. Both rules match, and the obligation's guard is U, so it is in force with finding U and reported unknown.
